summary: CI's objectives are declared over one `github.workflow-run` claim per completed Workspace CI run, so every member reads the same rows; the in-memory Workspace CI reading and the shipped `ci-duration`/`ci-count` objectives are gone

replay.detail: No projection changes; declared objectives evaluate the replicated claims in memory, as before.

schema.detail: New subject family `github-workflow-run` (`github-workflow-run/OWNER/REPO/RUN_ID`) and claim kind `github.workflow-run` v1 (system-only, once per subject, durable, at most 1 KiB): version, observer, repository, workflow, run_id, attempt, event, conclusion, head_sha, created_at, started_at, completed_at, duration_ms, flaky_tests, flakes. The GitHub plugin's manifest allows it as its third graph kind.

rules.detail: Interval and count indicators take `only "FIELD" "A" ...` (a sample or event is kept only when its claim has one of the values; left-out ones are counted with the excluded). An interval's `stop` may name its `start` kind when both read different `at=` fields, so one claim is the whole sample. The `ci-duration` and `ci-count` indicators are removed: `slo/objectives.kdl` no longer ships `merge-latency`, `ci-critical-path` or `flakes`, and no shipped objective opens a fault. `slo/fractal-ci.kdl` declares `fractal/merge-latency` (p50, p95 ≤ 10m over 1d), `fractal/ci-critical-path` (p95 ≤ 13m over 1d) and `fractal/flakes` (runs with a flake, max 0 an hour). Pull request runs of every conclusion are now recorded, so a flaky test in a failed or cancelled pull request run counts toward `fractal/flakes`; the shipped `flakes` row read only successful pull request runs.

compatibility.detail: Row ids move from `merge-latency/pNN`, `ci-critical-path/p95` and `flakes` to `fractal/merge-latency/pNN`, `fractal/ci-critical-path/p95` and `fractal/flakes`. Older builds refuse a `github.workflow-run` claim and an objective using `only` or a same-kind stop, so every member upgrades before `slo/fractal-ci.kdl` is applied and before a poller writes the kind.

downtime.detail: No runtime deployment or migration changes.

manual.detail: After every member upgrades: the CI rows' producer (agent/compoundingtech/st-o11y) activates the poller with its `main_performance_failures` subscription on `observer/github/compoundingtech/fractal`, and `fractal apply slo/fractal-ci.kdl` publishes the objectives.

recovery.detail: Retire the objectives to stop their evaluation; the claims stay as history. No member opens the shipped CI faults (`slo-objective/NODE/merge-latency/...`, `.../ci-critical-path/p95`, `.../flakes`) any more, and a member's start ends any of them still open with an `operational.recovered` that says the objective is retired; none was open when this shipped, because no member read Workspace CI (no `main_performance_failures` subscription existed).
